USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold firm at the current escalated posture — keep the newly-raised 25% tariffs on the $200B list and the Huawei/E.O. 13873 measures in place as leverage — but do not immediately push to the threatened ~$300B tariff list, which would hit consumer-facing goods and deepen the market selloff. Signal willingness to resume talks with Beijing (which has invited negotiators back and left June 1 room on its retaliation) and use the scheduled G-20 meeting as the venue to press for a deal. Do not roll back unilaterally while China has refused and retaliated.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: This is a genuine escalation peak: the U.S. raised List 3 tariffs from 10% to 25% on May 10 and moved against Huawei on May 15, and China retaliated with tariffs up to 25% on ~$60B of U.S. goods effective June 1, declaring it will 'never surrender' (event timeline, May 10/13/15; PBS/Reuters). The threat reading is material but not existential: markets priced real damage — the Dow fell ~617 pts (-2.4%), S&P -2.4%, Nasdaq -3.3% on May 13, with ~$1.1T of market value lost since the May 5 tweets, the 10-yr yield sliding from ~3.06% (Nov) to 2.37% (May 15), and the VIX spiking ~28% (country_health DGS10; web). Yet the U.S. economy remains resilient — consumer sentiment at 100, IP roughly flat — and the U.S. holds the leverage edge (larger economy, a $300B threat still on the table, entity list), so this rates ~+0.3, not existential. On action: we just executed maximal pressure and Trump has explicitly said 'no decision yet' on the $300B list (Guardian May 13), and both sides left negotiating room (delayed tariff phases, Beijing invitation, G-20), so the disciplined move is hold at current leverage rather than escalate into consumer-hitting territory or concede prematurely — hence a mildly firm action_score of -0.1 and 'hold'.
